evals.prompt: Wireshark is blocked on my work Mac. I have a capture at ~/Desktop/upload-fail.pcapng. Show me the TCP conversations and whether there were any resets.
evals.expected_output: Reads the file with a full-path tcpdump -r command, summarizes conversations and resets from the output, and states what tcpdump cannot provide compared with Wireshark (such as per-conversation byte totals).
assertions: Reads the file with /usr/sbin/tcpdump or /opt/homebrew/opt/tcpdump/bin/tcpdump using a full path, not a bare tcpdump
Every tcpdump read command places -r FILE before other options
Does not run, install or recommend Wireshark, tshark, mergecap or editcap
States at least one concrete gap versus Wireshark
Does not use sudo to read the file

evals.prompt: I'm on the VPN. Capture what Slack connects to while I open a channel, and tell me which connections go over the tunnel.
evals.expected_output: Runs discover.py, uses its app list, routes and notes to choose Apple tcpdump with -i pktap,all and a process metadata filter, hands the user one sudo capture block that writes to the per-user temp folder and prints the capture path, then waits for the pasted output before analysing.
assertions: Runs python3 scripts/discover.py before building the capture command
The capture command uses /usr/sbin/tcpdump with -i pktap,all
The capture command uses --apple-md-filter with a process name taken from discovery process_names
Does not run sudo itself; gives the user a block to run and asks for the pasted output
The capture path is built from getconf DARWIN_USER_TEMP_DIR, not $TMPDIR
Does not claim capture results before the user pastes output

evals.prompt: I ran tcpdump -k NP -i en0 and it says invalid option. I thought macOS tcpdump had process info?
evals.expected_output: Explains that a bare tcpdump resolves to the Homebrew build, which lacks Apple's -k option, and gives the same command with /usr/sbin/tcpdump.
assertions: Identifies that bare tcpdump resolves to Homebrew (from discovery or which/command -v)
Recommends /usr/sbin/tcpdump by full path
Does not suggest uninstalling, reinstalling or changing PATH as the fix
Any live-capture command is handed to the user rather than run by the agent

evals.prompt: My capture with --apple-md-filter "pid = 4567" got 0 packets. I restarted the app right before I started it.
evals.expected_output: Identifies the stale PID as the likely cause, reruns discovery to get current PIDs and process names, and gives a corrected filter (prefer process name or eproc/epid). States that zero packets does not mean the app was idle.
assertions: Names the app restart invalidating the PID as the likely cause
Reruns discover.py (or asks to) to get current PIDs or process names
Proposes a filter using proc/eproc or the new pid/epid
Does not claim the app sent no traffic

evals.prompt: Does DNS for intranet.example.com go through my VPN or out my Wi-Fi?
evals.expected_output: Runs discover.py with --target intranet.example.com, reports which interface the relevant nameservers and the target route via, labels this as a routing prediction, and offers a user-run capture on port 53 to confirm.
assertions: Runs discover.py with --target intranet.example.com
Reports the interface for the resolver nameservers from dns_resolvers
States that a route lookup predicts the path and a capture is needed to prove it
Any capture offered includes port 53 and is handed to the user
Does not suggest changing DNS, routes, hosts or VPN settings
